## 固定收益市場主線

10月7日美國公債盤中遭到拋售，隨後$390億的10年期公債標售需求強勁，吸引買盤在殖利率超過5%時進場，帶動債市回穩。10年期與30年期殖利率分別收在5.2815%及5.6599%，均與前收持平。這場標售暫時化解高能源價格與資金競爭帶來的新一波壓力，但並未使當日借款成本進一步下降。

聯準會9月會議紀錄顯示，官員普遍支持已實施的升息，多數預期年底前還會再升息。最新家庭部門數據凸顯政策的兩難：通膨預期升高，房貸申請與消費信貸成長卻轉弱。布蘭特原油收在每桶$101以上，美股自歷史高點回落，美元走強。

企業與主權借款人面對的融資環境更加分化。SpaceX擬籌措$400億購買晶片，消息拖累既有債券價格，但美國投資級債券整體利差變化不大。法國官員否定ECB立即介入的必要性，也否認改變發債策略的報導，法國公債因而吐回週二的部分漲幅。印度則近四年來首次升息，推高債券殖利率，卻未能止住盧比跌勢。

## 標售需求強勁，通膨壓力仍在

美國財政部10年期公債標售得標殖利率為5.300%，低於投標截止前的市場殖利率。投標倍數達2.77，創2016年以來最高；非交易商投資人取得97.5%的發行量，比重創新高。相較前次標售的4.834%，此次借款成本明顯提高，卻也吸引異常強勁的參與需求。

標售結果扭轉盤中走勢。據Bloomberg報導，10年期殖利率一度升至5.36%，隨後回落至約5.28%；30年期盤中曾突破5.7%。SMBC利率策略師Monty Gandhi表示，大型投資人開始覺得這些水準具有吸引力，殖利率在5%左右時就已著手回補空頭。瑞穗的Evelyne Gomez-Liechti認為，市場正權衡絕對殖利率的吸引力與尚未化解的油價衝擊。

當日殖利率曲線最終維持不變。2年期殖利率為4.7986%，5年期為5.0347%，2年與10年期利差為48.29個基點，2年與30年期利差為86.13個基點。不過，以一週變化來看，2年與5年期殖利率分別下降9.14及5.23個基點，10年期僅下降0.85個基點，30年期反而上升1.99個基點。同期間，2年與10年期利差擴大8.29個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大11.13個基點。市場對近期政策壓力的緩解，主要反映在較短天期，並未充分延伸至長端。

10年期實質殖利率維持2.9118%，損益兩平通膨率維持2.3697%。過去一個月，10年期名目殖利率上升49.85個基點，其中48.18個基點來自實質殖利率上升，通膨補償僅增加1.67個基點。這項較長期間的比較，支持美國財政部長Scott Bessent週三所說的觀點：經濟成長強勁與實質利率提高，是美國殖利率上升的主要原因。他預期伊朗衝突平息後，能源成本與利率將下降。

聯準會會議紀錄更完整交代官員開始緊縮的理由。19位與會者全數支持9月決定，FOMC投票委員也一致同意升息25個基點，將目標區間提高至3.75%至4%。許多與會者支持升息，是為了防範日益加劇的通膨壓力；另一批官員則依其經濟展望，認為有必要提高利率。多數人判斷，年底前可能仍適合再升息一次。

部分官員看到基礎經濟動能增強。儘管長天期美國公債殖利率上升，許多人仍認為金融情勢有利成長，理由包括股市上漲及企業債利差偏窄。9月升息前，部分官員認為政策利率不具限制性，或僅略具限制性。這也說明，市場借款成本上升，並未讓委員會認定緊縮程度已經足夠。

會議紀錄反映的是9月討論，10月政策預期則已受較新的官員發言影響。Bloomberg的會議紀錄報導指出，週三聯邦資金期貨反映10月27至28日會議升息25個基點的機率約20%，低於9月決策後數日的約70%。副主席Philip Jefferson與紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams近期主張耐心觀察，降低了立即採取下一步行動的急迫性，但控制通膨仍是政策展望的核心。

週三公布的通膨預期數據，使這項顧慮更為突出。9月消費者通膨預期由3.6%升至3.9%，高於預估的3.7%。紐約聯準銀行調查同時顯示，家庭對勞動市場的看法改善。家庭預期物價漲幅更高，對就業的評估卻較不悲觀，與利率敏感借款的萎縮形成不同訊號。

美國房貸銀行協會數據顯示，截至10月2日的一週，30年期固定房貸合約利率上升19個基點至7.49%，創2023年11月以來最高。利率已連續七週上升，近三週累計約升半個百分點，為2023年初以來最快的同期間升幅。房貸申請總量繼前週下降6%後，再減少4.2%；市場指數由213.6降至204.7，購屋申請指數由148.2降至145.1，轉貸指數由557.8降至515.8。

購屋申請減少2.1%，降至一年多來最低；轉貸申請下滑7.5%，延續8月中旬以來跌勢。較高利率同時壓抑新借款，以及以新房貸取代既有房貸的機會。8月消費信貸增加$82.8億，低於市場共識的$150億，也低於7月修正後的$177.4億。這些數據反映融資需求放緩，而非聯準會所關注的整體經濟活動普遍退縮。

中古車價格則提供另一項通膨降溫訊號。9月價格月減1.1%，前月下降0.9%；年減0.6%，前月仍年增0.4%。這一類商品價格改善，但家庭通膨預期升高，顯示個別商品價格與民眾對整體生活成本的預期並不相同。

週三報導的紐約聯準銀行研究，也區分了通膨率與物價水準。Mary Amiti、Sebastian Heise及David Weinstein發現，關稅使進口與生產者價格上升10%時，零售消費者價格上升5.6%。約三分之二的影響來自進口消費品，於一個月內直接傳導；其餘三分之一則透過國內生產者投入成本增加，或提高售價的空間擴大，間接傳導。後者沿供應鏈反映，需時六至十二個月。研究估計，關稅對通膨的貢獻在2026年2月達到高峰，預測至8月逐漸降至接近零，但消費品物價水準仍會高於原先。

能源情勢更難定論。布蘭特原油收漲0.52%至每桶$101.10，較一週前上漲3.13%，較一個月前上漲9.51%；WTI則下跌0.48%至$89.01。布蘭特盤中曾短暫突破$102，交易員一方面衡量伊朗攻擊油輪的影響，一方面觀察中東供應流量仍具韌性。沙烏地阿拉伯支持的部隊反攻胡塞武裝，則增添另一條戰線：聯軍宣稱在曼德海峽附近取得領土進展，武裝分子仍持續攻擊沙烏地城市與能源設施。華府不願把支援擴大至情報以外，並試圖控制葉門衝突。

EIA公布，截至10月2日的一週，原油庫存減少318.6萬桶，市場原預期增加170萬桶，前週則增加92.2萬桶。不過，成品油庫存不像預期緊張：汽油庫存增加38.2萬桶，原預期減少170萬桶；蒸餾油庫存僅減少4.2萬桶，原預期減少210萬桶。煉油廠原油加工量增加22.3萬桶，扭轉前週下降。官方數據因此同時呈現原油庫存意外減少，以及燃料庫存壓力小於預期。

股市回落幅度有限。標普500指數下跌0.22%至7,801.77，那斯達克100指數下跌0.21%，半導體股下跌1.15%。美元指數上升0.41%至102.25，黃金期貨下跌1.36%至每盎司$4,130.20。即使地緣政治風險仍高，計息資產可提供更高收益，加上美元轉強，仍對金價形成壓力。

策略師最新殖利率看法，顯示對後市仍有明顯分歧。高盛William Marshall維持10年期年底殖利率4.75%的預測，預期關稅與衝突相關的通膨壓力終將緩和。德意志銀行維持4.8%，但Matthew Raskin表示，基本面也可能合理支持5%至5.5%、甚至更高的區間。摩根士丹利同樣預測4.8%；其債市悲觀情境的5.25%已接近目前殖利率，而油價導致全球衰退，則是債市樂觀情境3.8%的依據。

巴克萊更傾向高利率持續，將2027年第3季10年期殖利率預測由5%上調至5.25%。Anshul Pradhan認為，只要經濟維持韌性，就看不到使殖利率跌破5%的明確催化因素；生產力提高也可能推升市場目前約3.5%的長期中性利率假設，進而使30年期殖利率朝6%靠攏。美國銀行的年底5%預測納入聯準會10月與12月升息，但Mark Cabana認為近期風險偏向殖利率上行。摩根大通預測5.05%；Jay Barry認為目前殖利率符合合理價值，但提醒客戶的存續期間部位整體呈淨超配，仍可能帶來進一步賣壓。在這些分歧之中，標售提供了具體的需求表現，並未使市場對殖利率最終落點形成共識。

## SpaceX融資計畫拖累既有債券

SpaceX正初步洽談籌措$400億購買Nvidia晶片，AI擴張的融資負擔直接反映在次級市場價格。Bloomberg報導，Pimco是評估這筆交易的投資人之一。《金融時報》則指出，融資約包括$100億銀行貸款及$300億投資級債務，由Apollo主導，預計2027年完成。

ICE Data Services數據顯示，SpaceX的5年期信用違約交換利差盤中最多上升16.2個基點至約197.1個基點，為6月開始活躍交易以來最高。紐約時間上午10時30分，2036年到期、票息5.875%的債券相對美國公債利差擴大12個基點至200個基點；這批證券6月作為$250億債務交易的一部分發行時，利差為140個基點。

Impax投資組合經理Tony Trzcinka認為，市場主要在反映SpaceX新增債務的規模與速度。他表示，新增借款可能需要更高殖利率才能吸引買盤，既有債券價格因此必須下跌，提供可競爭的報酬。

其他大型科技與媒體借款人的債券也走弱。Meta在2036年到期、票息5.25%的債券利差擴大7個基點至103個基點；Skydance票息8.75%的30年期債券利差擴大9個基點至339個基點，近期發行利差則為315個基點。不過，美國投資級債券整體利差收盤變化不大；高收益債利差小幅擴大，硬通貨新興市場債利差則明顯擴大。當日投資級債最顯著的跌勢集中在個別借款人，並非全市場一致擴大利差。

AI融資規模已相當龐大。據Bloomberg，今年全球超大型雲端業者、資料中心及其他AI基礎設施專案，透過投資級與高收益債券借款約$3,700億，2025年全年則約$1,250億。Coherence Credit Strategies的Sal Naro強調，基礎設施建設的規模，以及全球同時進行的程度，都前所未見。SpaceX計畫將在已大幅擴張的市場上，再增添一筆大型融資。

亞洲盤初另有獨立進展。《華爾街日報》報導，Broadcom正為與OpenAI合作的客製化AI晶片安排逾$500億融資，與先前報導、為Anthropic及其他客戶安排的$600億融資是不同專案。這則美國週三收盤後的消息，進一步擴大潛在融資供給。

投資人對AI風險的時點與側重也不一致。Ray Dalio週三在新加坡警告，利率上升，加上帳面財富需轉換為現金，正使AI榮景更接近轉折點。淡馬錫國際投資長Rohit Sipahimalani則將AI反轉，以及通膨推升債券利率，列為2027年的主要風險，但不認為AI行情即將瓦解。

Sipahimalani希望淡馬錫AI投資中，公開交易資產的比重由約一半提高至70%至75%，以便在產業變化時調整。他對流動性的偏好，同時伴隨公司計畫在2031年前，將AI占整體投資組合的比重由6%提高至最高15%。這項調整是在擴大AI曝險的同時，增加易於交易的持有部位，而非退出產業。

AI資金需求也影響其他公司的退出管道。Permira共同執行長Brian Ruder表示，市場預期規模龐大的AI上市案，正排擠私募股權支持企業的上市關注度。債務成本提高及商業模式不確定，使資本結構不再那麼積極；他表示，Permira平均槓桿為4.5倍，因此較不受這項調整影響。

美國銀行Savita Subramanian從不同角度比較資產估值。10年期美國公債可提供逾5%的殖利率，但她的團隊估值模型顯示，標普500未來十年的報酬可能達不到這一水準。她也警告，企業獲利預期極高，使股市容易受到不如預期的結果衝擊；另一方面，人口結構趨勢與AI最終可能帶來的通膨降溫，或可限制殖利率上升幅度。

## 法國公債再承壓，官員反對立即介入

法國10年期公債相對德國的利差收盤擴大12個基點至140個基點，吐回週二的部分漲幅；週三盤中法國10年期殖利率上升逾16個基點。財政部否認正將發債轉向較短天期的報導，央行官員也反對立即介入法國財政問題，債市再度承壓。

財政部表示，債務策略仍依投資人需求安排，並彈性選擇標售券種。部方承認，隨殖利率上升，主要交易商近月反映需求轉弱，因此減少了30年以上債券的發行。這是在原有策略下調整個別標售，而非改變整體策略。財政部長Roland Lescure的相關發言經報導後，利差曾短暫收窄，隨後回升；財政部澄清後，債券期貨仍維持跌勢。

法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin稱情勢嚴峻，但尚未滿足ECB介入條件。他主張國會通過預算，並承諾將赤字控制在經濟產出的5%以內，而非利用央行處理財政問題。他也回應總統候選人Jean-Luc Mélenchon威脅以叛國罪追究他的言論，表示即使對方當選，自己也不會辭職。這場交鋒使制度爭議更加明確，與債市新一輪跌勢並存。

ECB管理委員會另一位成員Primoz Dolenc在盧比安納提出不同側面的評估。他表示，目前利率保留了回應未來變化的彈性，決策將依通膨預期及相關風險而定。高能源價格與地緣政治不確定性，持續帶來通膨壓力。他強調，傳導保護工具（TPI）有明確適用條件，ECB也密切監控跨市場外溢對貨幣政策傳導的影響，但公共財政仍應由各國政府負責。

拋售開始吸引部分機構選擇性進場，但買方反應不一。Mediolanum的Niall Scanlon認為法國利差相對基本面擴大過頭，已解除低配，但還沒有足夠信心轉為超配。Amova的Steve Williams較一個月前更為看好，等待加碼機會。Aegon的Irina Kurochkina也認為買點可能逐漸接近，但希望波動先降下來。

這些評估出現在法德利差近期曾逼近160個基點之後。法國債券期貨未平倉量週一減少近5%，為2025年4月以來最大單日降幅之一，與投資人解除部位的情況相符。週三行情逆轉顯示，部分投資人對估值的看法改善，尚未消除價格不穩定。

法國對義大利公債利差，也達到Bloomberg自1992年開始統計以來最高。DWS的Vera Fehling認為，目前價格已反映風險，OAT與BTP之間的利差提供相當緩衝；State Street的Elliot Hentov則希望社會更廣泛接受減債。買盤回流所等待的條件，從足夠的價格補償、波動降低，到政治上願意整頓財政，各不相同。

主權債壓力明顯傳至歐洲銀行股。法國興業銀行與德意志銀行盤中跌逾5%，歐元區斯托克銀行指數最多下跌4%，所有成分股均下跌。該指數今年仍上漲12%，但已較8月高點回落逾8%。

Davide Silvestrini領導的摩根大通策略團隊認為，這主要是情緒與部位調整驅動的降風險操作。其基本情境並不預期殖利率大幅進一步上升，主權利差擴大對銀行資產負債表的直接損害也應有限；若利差持續擴大，存款結構及資產品質的變化可能更重要。他們區分了即時按市價評價的疑慮，以及透過融資與經濟逐漸發生的影響。

歐元走弱不只反映在兌美元匯率。歐元兌英鎊最多下跌0.4%至84.48便士，創2025年6月以來最低；兌日圓也接近一年低點。1個月期歐元兌英鎊風險逆轉，自2024年8月以來首次偏向英鎊。避險歐元兌日圓波動的成本，比避險美元兌日圓高出逾100個基點，差距為2025年3月以來首見。交易員除因美元走強調整匯率，也在交叉匯率中反映歐洲財政與政治疑慮。

義大利則另外考慮加強對本國債券市場基礎設施的控制。知情人士表示，國營貸款機構Cassa Depositi e Prestiti可能收購Euronext持有的MTS 63%股權，估值約€6億。討論部分源於歐盟擬推動單一泛歐營運商執照及歐洲證券及市場管理局（ESMA）監管，部分義大利官員擔心，這會削弱本國對政府債券流動性的監督。Euronext表示，MTS仍是其策略性業務，公司致力發展該平台。

## 印度升息，各國政策路徑分歧

印度央行一致同意將附買回利率提高25個基點至5.50%，更重要的政策訊號則是另一項以四票對兩票通過的決定：將中性立場改為漸進緊縮。總裁Sanjay Malhotra表示，這將是幅度較溫和、依數據而定的循環，而非預先設定的升息序列。他排除近期降息，後續升息或暫停將視成長與通膨而定。

印度央行將本財政年度通膨預測由5%上調至5.2%，成長預測由6.7%上調至7.1%。Malhotra指出，已有通膨普遍化的初步跡象，包括核心物價走強，以及消費籃子中更多品項承受壓力。8月通膨率4.82%、季風雨勢不佳，以及盧比貶值帶來的進口成本，都促成政策轉變。截至6月的季度經濟成長已達7.8%，成長預測提高也使央行在緊縮時有較強的經濟活動作為支撐。

印度10年期殖利率最多上升7個基點，稍後上升3個基點至7.22%。野村Sonal Varma認為，立場轉變偏鷹，意味著不只一次性的政策微調。SMBC的Jeff Ng認為連續升息的可能性很高，Emkay的Madhavi Arora則預期整個循環將升息75個基點。他們的判斷都著重於國內通膨擴散，以及全球融資環境收緊。

匯市反應卻較不利。盧比最多貶值0.4%至每美元96.85盧比，接近5月創下的96.9650歷史低點。Finrex的Anil Kumar Bhansali表示，部分交易員把漸進緊縮解讀為有限的升息循環，因而撤回原先對更大幅度回收流動性的預期。外國投資組合投資人與石油公司買進美元，也增添壓力。交易員表示，印度央行出售美元支撐匯價。

附買回利率提高之外，流動性傳導仍是另一項問題。先前海外印度人存款異常強勁流入，使銀行體系超額資金在9月達到創紀錄的₹11兆；10月6日已降至₹4.8兆。Malhotra承諾使隔夜借款成本與政策利率一致，並在本財政年度回收相當部分的剩餘流動性，但表示提高現金準備率是最不優先考慮的工具。隔夜利率仍低於附買回利率，IDFC First Bank的Gaura Sengupta認為，必須使市場借款成本向基準利率靠攏，升息才能有效發揮作用。

越南官員則描述了融資與通膨之間不同的權衡。副總裁Pham Thanh Ha表示，存款及放款利率承受上行壓力，但央行仍需維持企業取得信貸的能力。放款較年底增加11.59%，全年目標約15%。9月通膨率5.08%，超過政府原訂4.5%的上限，10%的成長目標卻又推動融資需求。官員承諾彈性運用政策、配合財政措施，並維持銀行流動性充足。

日本薪資數據為持續政策正常化提供新支撐。8月實質現金薪資，以排除房租的物價指標調整後年增1.5%，符合預期，且已連續八個月增加。基本薪資與名目薪資均成長3.8%；排除獎金、加班及抽樣扭曲的較穩定指標，則顯示全職員工薪資增加2.8%。名目薪資已連續七個月成長逾3%，為1992年以來最長紀錄。

購買力改善部分來自公用事業費用補貼，但瑞穗Ryosuke Katagi強調，名目薪資成長本身也相當穩健。野村Kohei Okazaki預期冬季獎金表現良好，中小企業加薪壓力也會持續。不過，消費仍脆弱，家庭支出截至7月已連續八個月下降。東京週三上午的交換市場反映，日本央行年底前再升息的機率為76%；多數經濟學家則預期10月30日會議維持利率不變。

首相高市早苗也提出新的財政調整條件：殖利率若出現超乎預期的急劇變動，可能促使政府修訂支出及收入計畫，但她不願指明匯率或殖利率水準。這項彈性與另一項提案並存，即從4月起，將食品及非酒精飲料銷售稅由8%降至1%，為期兩年。週三聯準會會議紀錄另披露，紐約聯準銀行在7月聯合干預日圓時，擔任財政代理人並使用美國財政部資金，未動用聯準會自身證券投資組合。

波蘭連續第七個月將基準利率維持在3.75%，符合全部34位受訪經濟學家的預期，政府紓緩燃料價格的措施已減輕短期通膨壓力。但10年期殖利率仍上升3個基點至6.28%；遠期利率協議反映，六個月內約升息兩次、一年內四次，每次25個基點。法國農業信貸銀行預期11月升息，以抑制第二輪效應。PKO Bank Polski則持不同看法，認為暫時性供給衝擊消退後，即使不升息，通膨在2027年底也會接近目標。

瑞典也呈現當前通膨與未來緊縮預期的差異。9月初估、排除能源的固定利率消費者物價指數（CPIF）年增率維持0.5%，低於分析師中位數及瑞典央行估計的0.7%；整體CPIF年增率升至1.5%，仍低於2%目標。Nordea的Torbjorn Isaksson預期，即使基礎通膨壓力溫和，央行仍將在11月升息，並於2月進一步升至2.25%。Swedbank則指出，商品成本與瑞典克朗走弱是未來物價壓力來源。

匈牙利財政部長對主權融資展望較為樂觀。Andras Karman預測，隨€164億歐盟資金解凍，2027年成長將由今年估計的1.7%加速至2.4%。他認為，殖利率進一步下降有賴可信的赤字削減及加入歐元區路徑，並承諾削減規模過大的國家合約以節省支出。債務管理機構主管Gergely Tardos表示，加入歐元區的政策方向已擴大投資人基礎，吸引更多長期買方，但核心市場殖利率上升使利率收斂更困難。OTP的Peter Csanyi補充，近期工業成長高度集中在BMW生產；成長是否夠廣泛，與融資展望改善是不同問題。

## 融資管道與債權條款拉開借款人差距

亞太美元債發行放緩，區域殖利率升至6.1%，為2024年以來最高。10月至今，尚無發行人完成聯合承銷美元債發行。第3季發行量下降10%至約$880億，銀行業者預期第4季相較去年同期約$400億，將持平或減少。巴克萊Dhruv Saigal表示，有餘裕的借款人正等待利率與市場情勢穩定，因此接下來較可能進行的是必要融資。

日本占區域第3季美元債發行量近40%，其次為印度16%及南韓15%；中國大陸占比略低於7%。日圓企業債殖利率約2.8%，將美元融資透過交換轉回日圓後，成本可能具有競爭力。最高評等中國企業則可在本地以低於1.8%的成本，取得年期不超過7年的融資。這些替代管道，使亞洲發行放緩的情況與美國大型AI債券融資供給有所不同。

亞洲資料中心主要仍透過貸款取得資金，今年聯貸交易達$326億，已超過2025年全年$215億。T. Rowe Price的Sheldon Chan則表示，資料中心業者對發債的興趣正在增加。美元殖利率提高雖延後一般發行案，區域融資組合仍在演變。

墨西哥本地市場形成對比。非銀行企業截至9月發債2,348億披索，已高於去年全年14%，並創Banorte自2004年統計以來的年度最高金額。國內利率下降、債務逐漸到期，以及退休金與保險資金成長，都支持企業借款。VALMEX的Yazmin Matus表示，CFE的200億披索發行及Grupo Lala的90億披索交易，定價利差分別較最初預估最多收窄35及25個基點。市場仍有選擇性：MercadoLibre的墨西哥放款子公司原目標籌措50億披索，最後募得37.5億披索，但仍表示滿意需求與定價。

迦納可可局自2023年貸款重整後首次重返國內融資市場，以11%票息發行33.9億塞地，相當於$2.89億。這是為9月25日開始的收成季安排163億塞地融資計畫的首筆發行。受到天候與作物疾病影響，可可局設定產量目標65萬噸，低於前一季交付的逾75萬噸。迦納支付農民的價格高於象牙海岸，可能吸引非正式跨境供應，增加購豆所需現金，也為此次重返發債市場增添具體的融資不確定性。

印尼航空Garuda Indonesia正尋求更多營運資金借款，並已與Pertamina協商延長付款期限，以因應油價與維修支出對復甦的壓力。公司計畫在未來六個月，將去年Danantara提供的$14億融資剩餘部分用於維修，並考慮燃油避險。6月現金為$6.24億，流動負債則為$16億。上半年營收雖成長16%至$18.0億，仍虧損$1.207億，使股東權益為負$5,220萬；維修支出增至原先的三倍以上，達$2.32億。營運能力改善之際，新融資仍是為了解決現金需求。

Hertz債權人在可能展開到期協商前，至少已組成兩個團體。擔保貸款人聘請Evercore與Gibson Dunn；另一團體包括同時持有擔保及無擔保債權的Canso，聘請Houlihan Lokey及Ropes & Gray。Hertz正與PJT合作，尋求延長債務期限。公司非車輛債務約$60億、車輛債務$127億，其中約$27億貸款在2028年到期。2028年6月到期的$12億定期貸款，交易價格約為面額的59.625%。第2季營收成長10%至$24億，流動性為$9.84億，但中古車疲弱、燃料成本與家庭收入壓力，仍限制業務表現。

Braskem面臨更迫近的決定，債權人已拒絕另一項涉及約$110億債務的重整提案。股東提出約$10億新股本，為後續增資提供承接保證，條件是大幅減債。債權人先前要求的$30億遭拒後，仍認為新條件不足。各方在10月9日前持續協商；若錯過期限，持有多數債權者可要求終止庭外重整程序，並可能導向破產。Petrobras是否願意作出具有法律拘束力的出資承諾，仍是爭議核心。

AMC再融資的新細節則呈現不同結果。其$39.7億交易已於週一完成，包含優先債券、第一順位及第二順位擔保貸款，簡化資本結構並延長五年的資金支應期間。德意志銀行困境債務交易部門，在優先融資推向更廣泛市場前，先承接$11.2億的次順位風險。週三新披露的銀行承諾，說明這家深度投機級借款人如何湊齊融資。

併購融資中的契約保護也有差異。Paramount Skydance為收購Warner Bros. Discovery安排的$520億融資，除投機級借款外，也包括$300億投資級債券。投資級證券對Paramount資產享有第一順位擔保債權，卻缺少高收益債市場收購融資常見、限制借款人行為的契約條款。優先受償與限制借款人未來行為，是不同的債權保護來源。

退出依然困難，私募市場結構也隨之改變。Partners Group旗下一檔€66億旗艦基金，贖回要求已達季度上限，公司計畫將其拆分：較舊資產供希望取得現金的投資人持有，較新資產留給繼續投資者。另一項PJT調查顯示，2026年上半年完成的單一資產延續基金中，29%採取超額績效分成（super-carry）安排，占比接近前一年同期三倍。較高分成仍以個別交易達到績效門檻為條件，有時要求內部報酬率30%，或至少達投入資本的三倍。Parthenon為持有Kroll Bond Rating Agency的工具籌得逾$17億，HarbourVest接受了其他投資人原先抵制的條件。在仍難以向投資人返還現金的市場中，具吸引力的資產擁有較強議價能力。

Weston家族的Wittington投資工具，已同意以含債務$89億收購Boots，與Fairfax合作並取得營運控制權。交易涵蓋英國與愛爾蘭零售業務及數項相關業務，Sycamore與Pessina家族則保留其他權益。這筆大型收購案宣布之際，英國零售業正面對通膨與勞動成本上升的壓力。

## 後續市場觀察

下一場美國公債需求考驗，是紐約時間10月8日下午1時的$220億30年期標售。週三10年期需求強勁，這次將觀察買盤是否延伸至一週以來殖利率仍上升的長端。隨後美國財政部將回購最多$60億、剩餘期限20至30年的債券。兩項操作不同：標售反映新發長天期債券的需求，回購則買進既有證券。

週四紐約時間上午8時30分公布的首次申請失業救濟人數，預估20萬人；持續申請預估171萬人，前值170.1萬人。在房貸借款轉弱、消費信貸成長放緩之後，這些數據將提供即時的勞動市場資訊。Christopher Waller預定週四發表談話，Alberto Musalem隨後於紐約時間下午1時40分發言，Susan Collins則在週五發言。官員可就9月會議紀錄之後的新資訊提出評估。週四第3季GDPNow更新預期維持3.7%，提供另一項以模型估計的成長觀察。

週五紐約時間上午10時公布密西根大學初步調查，將觀察週三家庭通膨預期上升是否也出現在另一項調查。消費者信心預估由48.1降至47.6；調查中的通膨預期指標預估由4.6%升至4.7%，5年期預期則由3.4%升至3.5%。市場對能源壓力會消退，還是需要進一步緊縮，仍有分歧，預期期間的差異也因此重要。10月14日的9月消費者物價數據，是聯準會會議前下一項主要通膨發布。

祕魯預定當地時間10月7日下午6時決策，晚於已結束的美國固定收益交易時段。13位受訪分析師中，九位預期升息25個基點至4.5%，四位預期不變。9月通膨率4.55%，以及聖嬰現象可能損害食物供應，是支持緊縮的理由。這次決策將決定上述壓力是否中斷降息循環。

法國財政部長週四在倫敦會見投資人，波蘭央行總裁則於華沙時間下午3時舉行記者會。前者可觀察發債策略澄清後的需求，後者可能釐清暫時性燃料價格紓緩與後續緊縮理由的差別。歐元區財長週四也將在盧森堡開會，預期正式啟動尋找Isabel Schnabel執行理事會接任者的程序。Braskem的10月9日期限則是另一項迫切的債權人決定，涉及資本支持及協商能否延續。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered from an intraday selloff on October 7 as a strongly received $39 billion 10-year auction brought buyers back at yields above 5%. The 10-year finished at 5.2815% and the 30-year at 5.6599%, both unchanged from the previous close. The auction interrupted renewed pressure from expensive energy and competition for capital without delivering a further daily decline in borrowing rates.

The Federal Reserve's September minutes showed broad support for the increase already delivered and a majority expecting another by year-end. New household data sharpened the trade-off: inflation expectations rose, while mortgage applications and consumer-credit growth weakened. Brent finished above $101 a barrel, U.S. equities slipped from records and the dollar strengthened.

Corporate and sovereign borrowers faced more differentiated conditions. SpaceX's proposed $40 billion chip financing sent its existing bonds lower, although broad U.S. investment-grade spreads were little changed. French government debt surrendered part of Tuesday's recovery as officials rejected both an immediate ECB intervention and reports of a changed issuance strategy. India's first rate increase in nearly four years, meanwhile, lifted bond yields but failed to arrest the rupee's decline.

## A Strong Auction Meets Persistent Inflation Pressure

The Treasury's 10-year sale cleared at 5.300%, below the yield prevailing before the bidding deadline. Bid-to-cover reached 2.77, its highest since 2016, and non-dealer investors received a record 97.5% of the offering. Those measures showed unusually strong participation at a much higher borrowing cost than the previous auction's 4.834%.

The result changed the course of the session. Bloomberg's trading account put the 10-year yield as high as 5.36% before it retreated toward 5.28%; the 30-year had traded above 5.7%. SMBC rates strategist Monty Gandhi said larger investors were finding these levels appealing, having begun unwinding shorts around 5%. Mizuho's Evelyne Gomez-Liechti described a market balancing attractive outright yields against an oil shock that remained unresolved.

The daily curve ended unchanged. The two-year yielded 4.7986% and the five-year 5.0347%, leaving 2s10s at 48.29 basis points and 2s30s at 86.13. Over the week, however, the two-year yield was down 9.14 basis points and the five-year down 5.23, against a decline of only 0.85 at 10 years and a rise of 1.99 at 30 years. The 2s10s spread had widened 8.29 basis points over that interval, while 2s30s was 11.13 wider. Relief over near-term policy had traveled much less far along the curve.

At 10 years, the real yield held at 2.9118% and breakeven inflation at 2.3697%. The month's 49.85-basis-point rise in the nominal yield comprised a 48.18-basis-point increase in the real yield and only 1.67 in inflation compensation. That longer comparison gives substance to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's Wednesday argument that strong growth and higher real rates were central to the U.S. yield rise. His expectation that energy costs and rates would decline once the Iran conflict subsided remained conditional on that conflict easing.

The Fed minutes supplied a more detailed account of why officials had begun tightening. All 19 participants supported September's decision, and FOMC voters unanimously raised the target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4%. Many participants favored the move as protection against intensifying inflation pressure; another group judged higher rates necessary on their economic outlook. Most thought a further increase would probably be appropriate by year-end.

Several officials saw stronger underlying economic momentum. Many also judged financial conditions supportive of growth despite the rise in long Treasury yields, pointing to higher equities and narrow corporate spreads. Before the September increase, several considered the policy rate either nonrestrictive or only mildly restrictive. That assessment explains why higher market borrowing costs had not persuaded the committee that sufficient restraint was already in place.

The minutes described the September discussion rather than a new October commitment. Federal funds futures on Wednesday assigned roughly a 20% chance to a quarter-point increase at the October 27-28 meeting, down from about 70% in the days after September's decision, according to Bloomberg's minutes account. More recent calls for patience from Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams had reduced the urgency of the next move, while leaving inflation control central to the policy outlook.

Wednesday's inflation-expectations release reinforced that concern. September consumer inflation expectations increased to 3.9% from 3.6%, above the 3.7% forecast. The New York Fed survey also showed improved sentiment toward the labor market. Households were expecting more inflation even as their labor assessment became less pessimistic, a combination distinct from the contraction in interest-sensitive borrowing.

Mortgage Bankers Association figures showed the 30-year fixed contract rate rising 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, its highest since November 2023. It was the seventh consecutive weekly increase and a rise of about half a percentage point in three weeks, the fastest such increase since early 2023. Total mortgage applications fell 4.2%, following a 6% decline. The market index dropped to 204.7 from 213.6, the purchase index to 145.1 from 148.2 and the refinance index to 515.8 from 557.8.

Purchase applications fell 2.1% to their lowest level in more than a year, while refinancing declined 7.5%, extending a slide that began in mid-August. Higher rates were constraining both new borrowing and the opportunity to replace existing mortgages. August consumer credit increased $8.28 billion, below the $15 billion consensus and a revised $17.74 billion increase in July. These releases showed slowing financing demand, rather than a generalized retreat in the activity that had concerned the Fed.

Used-car prices provided a separate disinflationary observation. September prices fell 1.1% month on month after a 0.9% decline and were 0.6% lower year on year, following a 0.4% annual increase. The improvement in that category sat alongside higher household inflation expectations, preserving a distinction between particular goods prices and the broader expected cost of living.

New York Fed research reported Wednesday offered another distinction between inflation and price levels. Mary Amiti, Sebastian Heise and David Weinstein found that a 10% tariff-driven increase in import and producer prices raised retail consumer prices by 5.6%. About two-thirds of the effect came directly through imported consumer goods, within a month; the remaining third came indirectly through domestic producers' input costs or greater scope to raise prices. The indirect effect took six to 12 months to pass through supply chains. Their analysis put the inflation contribution's peak in February 2026 and projected it fading toward zero by August, while leaving consumer-goods price levels higher.

Energy remained less settled. Brent finished up 0.52% at $101.10 a barrel, 3.13% higher over the week and 9.51% above its month-earlier level. WTI declined 0.48% to $89.01. Earlier, Brent had briefly exceeded $102 as traders weighed Iranian attacks on tankers against resilient Middle Eastern flows. Saudi-backed forces' counter-offensive against the Houthis added a separate front: the coalition reported territorial gains near Bab el-Mandeb, while militants continued attacking Saudi cities and energy sites. Washington was reluctant to expand support beyond intelligence and sought to contain the Yemen conflict.

The EIA reported a 3.186 million-barrel crude draw for the week ended October 2, against expectations of a 1.7 million-barrel increase and a previous 0.922 million-barrel build. Product stocks were less tight than expected. Gasoline inventories rose 0.382 million barrels against an expected 1.7 million-barrel draw, and distillates declined only 0.042 million against a projected 2.1 million-barrel fall. Refinery crude runs increased 0.223 million, reversing the previous week's decline. The official release therefore combined an unexpected crude draw with smaller pressure on fuel inventories than the forecasts implied.

The equity reversal was modest: the S&P 500 fell 0.22% to 7,801.77 and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.21%, while semiconductor shares declined 1.15%. The Dollar Index rose 0.41% to 102.25, and gold futures fell 1.36% to $4,130.20 an ounce. Stronger income available on interest-bearing assets and a firmer dollar weighed on bullion even while geopolitical risks remained elevated.

Strategists' new yield assessments reflected substantial disagreement about what would follow. Goldman Sachs' William Marshall maintained a 4.75% year-end 10-year forecast, expecting tariff and conflict-related inflation pressures eventually to moderate. Deutsche Bank retained 4.8%, although Matthew Raskin said fundamentals could plausibly support a 5%-5.5% range or higher. Morgan Stanley also projected 4.8%; its 5.25% bearish scenario was already around current yields, while an oil-induced global recession underpinned its 3.8% bullish scenario.

Barclays took a more persistent view of high rates, raising its Q3 2027 10-year forecast to 5.25% from 5%. Anshul Pradhan saw no clear catalyst for a move below 5% while the economy remained resilient and argued that stronger productivity could lift the market's roughly 3.5% long-run neutral-rate assumption, taking the 30-year toward 6%. Bank of America's 5% year-end forecast incorporated October and December Fed increases, but Mark Cabana judged the immediate risks tilted toward higher yields. JPMorgan projected 5.05%; Jay Barry regarded current yields as fair value while warning that clients' net overweight in duration left room for further selling. The auction supplied a concrete demand result within that disagreement, not agreement on where yields would settle.

## SpaceX's Financing Plans Reprice Existing Debt

SpaceX's early-stage discussions to raise $40 billion for Nvidia chips brought the AI expansion's financing burden directly into secondary-market prices. Bloomberg reported Pimco among the investors examining the transaction. The Financial Times described approximately $10 billion of bank loans and $30 billion of investment-grade debt, with Apollo leading financing expected to close in 2027.

The company's five-year credit-default swaps rose as much as 16.2 basis points to around 197.1, the highest intraday cost since active trading began in June, according to ICE Data Services. Its 5.875% bonds due in 2036 widened 12 basis points to 200 over Treasuries at 10:30 a.m. New York time. That compared with 140 basis points when the securities were sold in June as part of a $25 billion debt transaction.

Impax portfolio manager Tony Trzcinka attributed the adjustment primarily to how much debt SpaceX was adding and how quickly. Additional borrowing would probably need a higher yield to attract buyers, he said, requiring existing bonds to fall in price to offer competitive returns. The reaction concerned the expected funding burden and prospective new-issue pricing before the proposed financing had been agreed.

Other large technology and media borrowers also weakened. Meta's 5.25% notes due in 2036 widened 7 basis points to 103, while Skydance's 8.75% 30-year bonds widened 9 to 339, compared with their recent issue spread of 315. Broad U.S. investment-grade spreads nevertheless finished little changed. U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly, and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. The day's most conspicuous high-grade losses were concentrated in particular borrowers rather than a uniform widening across the market.

The financing scale was substantial. Hyperscalers, data centers and other AI infrastructure projects had borrowed around $370 billion worldwide through investment-grade and high-yield bonds this year, against about $125 billion during all of 2025, according to Bloomberg. Coherence Credit Strategies' Sal Naro emphasized the unprecedented size and worldwide simultaneity of the infrastructure buildout. SpaceX's proposal would add another large financing to an already expanded market.

In a separate development reported in the early Asian session, the Wall Street Journal said Broadcom was arranging more than $50 billion for its custom AI chip with OpenAI. That project is distinct from the previously reported $60 billion financing for Anthropic and other customers. The new report extended the prospective funding pipeline after Wednesday's U.S. close.

Investor assessments also differed in timing and emphasis. Ray Dalio warned Wednesday in Singapore that rising rates and the need to convert paper wealth into cash were bringing the AI boom closer to a breaking point. Temasek International CIO Rohit Sipahimalani identified an AI reversal and inflation-driven bond-rate pressure as major risks for 2027, but did not regard an unwinding as imminent.

Sipahimalani wanted publicly traded investments to represent 70%-75% of Temasek's AI exposure, up from around half, to make adjustment easier as the industry changed. That liquidity preference accompanied the firm's plan to increase AI's overall portfolio allocation from 6% to as much as 15% by 2031. The intended shift was toward more readily tradable holdings within an expanding exposure, rather than withdrawal from the sector.

The demand for AI capital was also affecting other companies' exits. Permira co-CEO Brian Ruder said enormous anticipated AI listings were crowding out attention for private-equity-backed offerings. Higher debt costs and uncertainty about business models were making capital structures less aggressive; he said Permira's average leverage of 4.5 times left it less exposed to that adjustment.

Bank of America's Savita Subramanian framed the competing asset-market valuations differently. A 10-year Treasury offered more than 5%, while her team's valuation framework suggested S&P 500 returns over the next decade might not reach that level. That comparison was a model assessment of future equity returns, not a realized performance gap. She also warned that exceptionally high earnings expectations left equities vulnerable to disappointment, while viewing demographic trends and eventual AI disinflation as possible limits on how far yields could rise.

## France Loses Ground as Officials Resist Intervention

France's 10-year premium over Germany closed 12 basis points wider at 140, reversing part of Tuesday's relief. French 10-year yields rose more than 16 basis points in Wednesday's trading. The renewed pressure came as the finance ministry disputed a report that it was changing issuance toward shorter maturities and central bankers rejected immediate intervention to address the country's fiscal problems.

The ministry said its debt strategy continued to follow investor demand, using flexibility over the bonds selected for auctions. It acknowledged having issued less debt beyond 30 years because primary dealers had reported weaker demand over recent months as yields rose. The distinction was between changing the overall strategy and adapting individual auctions within it. The spread briefly narrowed after the reported remarks from Finance Minister Roland Lescure, then recovered; bond futures remained lower after the ministry's clarification.

Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin called the situation serious but said conditions for ECB intervention were not met. His prescription was for parliament to pass a budget and commit to a deficit no higher than 5% of output, rather than use the central bank to manage fiscal problems. He also said he would not resign if Jean-Luc Mélenchon won the presidency, responding to the candidate's threat to pursue him for treason. That exchange made the institutional dispute explicit alongside the renewed bond losses.

Fellow Governing Council member Primoz Dolenc gave a separate assessment in Ljubljana. Existing rates provided flexibility to respond to future developments, he said, with decisions dependent on inflation expectations and associated risks. High energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty were sustaining inflation pressure. He emphasized both the defined conditions attached to the Transmission Protection Instrument and the ECB's close monitoring of cross-market spillovers into monetary transmission, while assigning responsibility for public finances to national governments.

The selloff was beginning to attract selective institutional interest, but not a common response. Mediolanum's Niall Scanlon had closed an underweight in France because he believed spreads had overshot fundamentals, without becoming sufficiently confident to move overweight. Amova's Steve Williams was more constructive than a month earlier and awaited opportunities to add. Aegon's Irina Kurochkina also saw a possible buying opportunity approaching but wanted volatility to subside.

Those responses followed a recent French-German spread peak near 160 basis points. French bond-futures open interest fell almost 5% on Monday, one of its largest daily declines since April 2025, consistent with positions being closed. Wednesday's reversal showed that the improvement in some investors' valuation assessments had not removed price instability.

France's spread over Italy was at a record in Bloomberg's series beginning in 1992. DWS's Vera Fehling regarded current prices as reflecting the risks and the OAT-BTP gap as a substantial buffer. State Street's Elliot Hentov instead wanted wider public acceptance of debt reduction. The differing conditions for renewed demand ranged from price compensation to reduced volatility and political willingness to consolidate.

The renewed sovereign pressure spread visibly to European bank shares. Societe Generale and Deutsche Bank fell more than 5% in intraday trading, while the Euro Stoxx Banks Index lost as much as 4%, with every constituent lower. The gauge remained up 12% for the year but had retreated more than 8% from its August high.

JPMorgan strategists led by Davide Silvestrini regarded the move principally as sentiment- and positioning-driven de-risking. Their base case did not envisage substantially higher yields, and they expected limited direct balance-sheet damage from wider sovereign spreads. Changes in deposit mix and asset quality could matter more if the widening persisted. Their assessment distinguished immediate mark-to-market concerns from slower effects through funding and the economy.

The euro's weakness became broader than its dollar pair. It fell as much as 0.4% against sterling to 84.48 pence, the lowest since June 2025, and approached its weakest level in a year against the yen. One-month euro-sterling risk reversals favored the pound for the first time since August 2024. Hedging euro-yen volatility cost over 100 basis points more than hedging dollar-yen swings, a gap not seen since March 2025. Traders were expressing European fiscal and political concern in crosses as well as against a strengthening dollar.

Italy separately began considering greater national control over its debt-market infrastructure. People familiar with discussions said state lender Cassa Depositi e Prestiti could buy Euronext's 63% stake in MTS, valued at roughly EUR600 million. The proposal responds partly to EU plans for a single pan-European operator license and ESMA supervision, which some Italian officials fear could weaken national oversight of government-bond liquidity. Euronext said MTS remained strategic to its business and it was committed to developing the platform. The discussions concern ownership and supervision of the main wholesale trading venue, not a completed transfer.

## India Tightens While Other Policy Paths Diverge

The Reserve Bank of India unanimously raised its repo rate 25 basis points to 5.50%, but the more consequential guidance came in a separate four-to-two vote to replace a neutral stance with calibrated tightening. Governor Sanjay Malhotra described a milder, data-dependent cycle rather than a predetermined sequence. He ruled out near-term cuts, leaving further increases or pauses dependent on growth and inflation.

The RBI raised its fiscal-year inflation projection to 5.2% from 5% and its growth forecast to 7.1% from 6.7%. Malhotra cited early signs of generalized inflation, including firmer core prices and pressure across more of the consumer basket. August inflation of 4.82%, weak monsoon conditions and imported costs from the rupee's decline were contributing to the shift. The higher growth forecast gave the bank a stronger activity backdrop for tightening, with June-quarter expansion already at 7.8%.

India's 10-year yield rose as much as 7 basis points, later trading 3 higher at 7.22%. Nomura's Sonal Varma judged the stance change hawkish, signaling more than a one-off recalibration. SMBC's Jeff Ng saw a strong possibility of consecutive increases, and Emkay's Madhavi Arora expected 75 basis points across the cycle. Their assessments emphasized both broadening domestic inflation and tighter global financing conditions.

The currency reaction was less favorable. The rupee weakened as much as 0.4% to 96.85 per dollar, approaching its May record low of 96.9650. Finrex's Anil Kumar Bhansali said some traders interpreted calibrated tightening as a limited hiking cycle and unwound expectations of stronger liquidity withdrawal. Foreign-portfolio and oil-company dollar buying added pressure. Traders said the RBI sold dollars to support the currency.

Liquidity transmission remained a separate issue from the repo-rate increase. Excess banking cash stood at 4.8 trillion rupees on October 6, below September's 11 trillion record after unusually strong diaspora deposit inflows. Malhotra pledged to align overnight borrowing costs with the policy rate and drain a significant share of the surplus during the fiscal year, calling an increase in the cash reserve ratio the least-preferred tool. With overnight rates below repo, IDFC First Bank's Gaura Sengupta argued that bringing market borrowing costs toward the benchmark was necessary for an increase to work effectively.

Vietnam's officials described a different balance between funding and inflation. Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha said deposit and lending rates were under upward pressure while the central bank needed to preserve business access to credit. Lending had increased 11.59% from year-end against an approximately 15% annual target. September inflation of 5.08% exceeded the government's intended 4.5% cap, even as its 10% growth objective drove demand for financing. Officials promised flexible policy, fiscal coordination and adequate bank liquidity; they did not announce a rate increase.

Japanese wages added fresh support for continued normalization. August real cash earnings, adjusted for inflation excluding rents, rose 1.5% year on year, matching forecasts and extending gains to an eighth month. Base salaries and nominal wages both increased 3.8%, while the more stable measure excluding bonuses, overtime and sampling distortions rose 2.8% for full-time workers. Nominal gains had exceeded 3% for seven months, their longest such run since 1992.

The improvement in purchasing power owed partly to utility subsidies, but Mizuho's Ryosuke Katagi emphasized solid nominal wage growth. Nomura's Kohei Okazaki expected favorable winter bonuses and continuing pay pressure at smaller firms. Consumption remained fragile, with household spending having fallen for eight months through July. Wednesday morning Tokyo swaps assigned a 76% probability to a further BOJ increase by year-end, while most economists expected no change at the October 30 meeting.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also offered a new fiscal condition: unexpectedly sharp yield moves could prompt revisions to spending and revenue plans. She declined to identify specific currency or yield levels. That flexibility sits beside the proposed reduction in food and nonalcoholic-beverage sales tax from 8% to 1% for two years starting in April. Wednesday's Fed minutes separately disclosed that the New York Fed had used Treasury funds, acting as fiscal agent, in July's joint yen intervention; the Fed's own securities portfolio was not involved. The disclosure clarified the financing of the earlier operation rather than announcing another intervention.

Poland held its benchmark at 3.75% for a seventh month, as all 34 surveyed economists expected, after government fuel-price relief tempered immediate inflation pressure. Its 10-year yield nevertheless rose 3 basis points to 6.28%, and forward-rate agreements implied roughly two quarter-point increases in six months and four within a year. Credit Agricole expected a November increase to contain second-round effects. PKO Bank Polski disagreed, arguing that temporary supply shocks would leave inflation close to target by late 2027 without higher rates.

Sweden supplied another distinction between current inflation and prospective tightening. Preliminary September CPIF excluding energy stayed at 0.5% annually, below the 0.7% analyst median and Riksbank estimate. Headline CPIF rose to 1.5%, still below the 2% target. Nordea's Torbjorn Isaksson expected a November increase despite modest underlying pressure, followed by a rise to 2.25% in February. Swedbank pointed to commodity costs and a weaker krona as sources of future pressure.

Hungary's finance minister offered a more favorable sovereign funding outlook. Andras Karman projected growth accelerating to 2.4% in 2027 from an estimated 1.7% this year, supported by the release of EUR16.4 billion in EU funding. He linked further yield declines to a credible deficit-reduction and euro-accession path and promised savings from oversized state contracts. Debt-agency chief Gergely Tardos said the euro narrative had broadened the investor base toward longer-term buyers, while warning that higher core-market yields complicated convergence. OTP's Peter Csanyi added that recent industrial growth was concentrated heavily in BMW production, making its breadth a separate issue from the improving financing narrative.

## Funding Access and Creditor Terms Separate Borrowers

Asia-Pacific dollar issuance was slowing as regional yields reached 6.1%, their highest since 2024. No issuer had completed a syndicated dollar bond sale so far in October. Third-quarter volume fell 10% to about $88 billion, and bankers expected Q4 issuance flat or lower against approximately $40 billion a year earlier. Barclays' Dhruv Saigal said borrowers with discretion were waiting for rates and market conditions to stabilize, leaving necessary financing more likely to proceed.

Japan supplied almost 40% of the region's third-quarter dollar volume, followed by India at 16% and South Korea at 15%; mainland China accounted for just under 7%. Yen corporate yields near 2.8% made dollar borrowing potentially competitive after swapping proceeds home. Top-rated Chinese companies could instead obtain local financing below 1.8% at maturities of seven years or less. Those alternatives helped differentiate the regional slowdown from the large U.S. AI-driven bond pipeline.

Asian data-center finance was still primarily reaching lenders through loans: $32.6 billion of syndicated transactions this year already exceeded 2025's $21.5 billion total. T. Rowe Price's Sheldon Chan nevertheless reported increasing interest from data-center companies in bond issuance. The region's financing mix was evolving even while higher dollar yields delayed conventional offerings.

Mexico's domestic market presented a contrast. Non-bank companies issued 234.8 billion pesos through September, 14% above the whole of last year's total and the largest annual amount in Banorte's series beginning in 2004. Lower domestic rates, approaching maturities and growth in pension and insurance capital supported borrowing. VALMEX's Yazmin Matus said CFE's 20 billion-peso offering and Grupo Lala's 9 billion-peso transaction priced as much as 35 and 25 basis points tighter than initially projected. Selectivity remained: MercadoLibre's Mexican lending unit raised 3.75 billion pesos against a 5 billion target, while expressing satisfaction with demand and pricing.

Ghana's Cocoa Board returned to domestic fundraising for the first time since its 2023 loan restructuring, selling 3.39 billion cedis, or $289 million, at an 11% coupon. The sale begins a 16.3 billion-cedi program for the harvest that started September 25. The board targets 650,000 tons of production, below more than 750,000 delivered in the previous season because of weather and crop disease. Ghana's higher farmer price relative to Ivory Coast could attract unofficial cross-border supplies and increase the cash needed to purchase beans, adding a specific financing uncertainty to the return of issuance.

Garuda Indonesia was seeking additional working-capital debt and had negotiated longer payment terms with Pertamina as oil and maintenance expenses strained its recovery. It planned to spend the remainder of last year's $1.4 billion Danantara financing on maintenance over the next six months and was considering fuel hedging. June cash of $624 million compared with $1.6 billion of current liabilities. A first-half loss of $120.7 million, despite 16% revenue growth to $1.80 billion, left equity at a $52.2 million deficit. Maintenance spending had more than tripled to $232 million. The new funding effort addressed cash needs despite improving operating capacity.

Hertz creditors were organizing into at least two groups ahead of possible maturity negotiations. Secured lenders retained Evercore and Gibson Dunn, while a group including Canso, which owns secured and unsecured claims, engaged Houlihan Lokey and Ropes & Gray. Hertz was working with PJT to extend obligations. It had approximately $6 billion of non-vehicle debt and $12.7 billion of vehicle debt, including about $2.7 billion of loans due in 2028. Its $1.2 billion June 2028 term loan traded around 59.625 cents on the dollar. Second-quarter revenue rose 10% to $2.4 billion and liquidity stood at $984 million, but used-car weakness, fuel costs and pressure on household income continued to constrain the business.

Braskem faced a nearer decision after creditors rejected another restructuring proposal for roughly $11 billion of debt. Shareholders offered about $1 billion of fresh equity to backstop a follow-on sale, conditional on substantial debt reduction. Creditors regarded the terms as insufficient, after their earlier request for $3 billion had been rejected. Talks continued before October 9; missing the deadline would allow a creditor majority to seek dissolution of the out-of-court process and could lead to bankruptcy, rather than automatically changing the proceedings. Petrobras's willingness to make an enforceable capital commitment remained central to the disagreement.

Fresh details of AMC's refinancing showed a different outcome. Its $3.97 billion transaction closed Monday with senior notes and first- and second-lien loans, simplifying the capital structure and extending its runway by five years. Deutsche Bank's distressed desk took $1.12 billion of junior risk before the senior financing reached the wider market. The newly reported bank commitment explained how a deeply speculative-grade borrower secured the completed package; it was not another Wednesday closing.

Contract protection also differed within acquisition finance. Paramount Skydance's $52 billion funding package for Warner Bros. Discovery included $30 billion of investment-grade bonds alongside speculative-grade borrowing. The high-grade securities had first-lien claims on Paramount assets but lacked debt terms commonly used in junk-market buyouts. Priority in repayment and restrictions on future borrower behavior were separate sources of creditor protection.

Private-market structures were changing as exits remained difficult. Partners Group planned to divide a EUR6.6 billion flagship fund between older assets for investors seeking cash and newer holdings for those remaining, after redemption requests reached the quarterly limit. Separately, PJT found super-carry arrangements in 29% of single-asset continuation funds closed during H1 2026, almost triple the year-earlier share. Higher payouts remained contingent on deal-specific performance thresholds, sometimes a 30% internal rate of return or at least three times invested capital. Parthenon raised more than $1.7 billion for a vehicle holding Kroll Bond Rating Agency after HarbourVest accepted terms other investors had resisted. The stronger negotiating position applied to coveted assets within a market still struggling to return cash.

The Weston family's Wittington vehicle agreed to acquire Boots for $8.9 billion including debt, partnering with Fairfax and taking operational control. The transaction covers the UK and Irish retail operations and several related businesses, while Sycamore and the Pessina family retain other interests. It supplies a substantial announced ownership change against inflation and rising labor-cost pressure in British retail.

## Forward Market Significance

The next Treasury demand test is the $22 billion 30-year auction on October 8 at 1 p.m. New York time. It extends Wednesday's strong reception at 10 years into the maturity where weekly yields have continued rising. A subsequent Treasury buyback will purchase as much as $6 billion of bonds maturing in 20 to 30 years. The auction and buyback are distinct operations: the former establishes demand for new long-duration supply, while the latter purchases existing securities.

Thursday's initial claims release, at 8:30 a.m. New York time, is expected at 200,000, with continuing claims at 1.710 million against 1.701 million previously. The releases will add a timely labor reading after weaker mortgage borrowing and slower consumer-credit growth. Christopher Waller is scheduled to speak Thursday, followed by Alberto Musalem at 1:40 p.m. New York time; Susan Collins speaks Friday. Their assessments can address information newer than the September minutes. Thursday's Q3 GDPNow update is expected to remain at 3.7%, providing a separate model-based growth observation.

Friday's preliminary Michigan survey, at 10 a.m. New York time, will test whether Wednesday's increase in household inflation expectations extends into another survey. Sentiment is expected at 47.6 after 48.1. Forecasts put the survey's inflation-expectations measure at 4.7% after 4.6% and its five-year measure at 3.5% after 3.4%. The horizon distinction matters alongside the disagreement over whether energy pressure will fade or require further restraint. September consumer-price data on October 14 remains the next major inflation release before the Fed meeting.

Peru's decision was scheduled for October 7 at 6 p.m. local time, after the completed U.S. fixed-income session. Nine of 13 surveyed analysts expected a 25-basis-point increase to 4.5%, with four forecasting no change. September inflation of 4.55% and prospective El Nino damage to food supplies underpin the tightening case. The decision would determine whether those pressures interrupt the easing cycle; no realized outcome was established by the decision preview.

France's finance minister meets investors in London Thursday, while Poland's governor holds his news conference at 3 p.m. Warsaw time. The first offers a test of demand after France's issuance clarification; the second may distinguish temporary fuel relief from the case for later tightening. Euro-area finance ministers also meet Thursday in Luxembourg, with a formal search for Isabel Schnabel's executive-board replacement expected to begin. Braskem's October 9 deadline is a separate, immediate creditor decision over capital support and the continuation of negotiations.

In the early Asian session Thursday, WTI rose 0.8% to $88.98 in Bloomberg's market account, while Australia's 10-year yield declined 2 basis points to 5.38%. Those later moves opened the next session with renewed energy pressure but some local duration demand, after Wednesday's U.S. auction had demonstrated that high absolute yields could still draw substantial buying.

overall_summary.headline: Strong 10-year auction demand reverses the Treasury selloff, leaving daily yields unchanged
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries recovered from an intraday selloff after the $39 billion 10-year auction cleared at 5.300%, with the strongest bid-to-cover since 2016 and a record 97.5% allocation to non-dealer investors. The 10-year finished unchanged at 5.2815%, and the 30-year was unchanged at 5.6599%. The curve also held steady, although weekly relief remained concentrated in shorter maturities. Real yields and breakevens were unchanged on the day; higher real yields accounted for 48.18 basis points of the month's 49.85-basis-point increase in the nominal 10-year yield.

The September Fed minutes showed unanimous support for the rate increase already delivered and a majority expecting another by year-end. Household inflation expectations rose to 3.9%, while mortgage applications and consumer-credit growth weakened. Brent closed above $101 a barrel, leaving the energy shock unresolved despite strong demand for Treasuries at higher yields.

SpaceX's proposed $40 billion chip financing pushed its existing bonds lower, while broad U.S. investment-grade spreads remained little changed; high-yield spreads widened modestly and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened noticeably. France's 10-year premium over Germany widened 12 basis points to 140 as officials rejected immediate ECB intervention and denied a change in issuance strategy. India's 25-basis-point repo-rate increase to 5.50% lifted bond yields but did not halt the rupee's decline. The next U.S. duration-demand test is Thursday's 30-year auction.
